text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Free Democrat leader Ivan Peto, explaining he assumes political responsibility for the activity of party members, offered his resignation after it was revealed that a party member is involved in the recent privatisation scandal. Observers believe it could seriously mar the Free Democrats' negotiating positions at today's coalition consultation with the Socialist Party. Prime Minister Gyula Horn ruled out a coalition crisis. @

- Tamas Deutsch, the Young Democrat chairman of the parliamentary commission established Tuesday to investigate the privatisation scandal, said that Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze will "obviously" be among the first persons to be heard by the commission.

- Lawyer Marta Tocsik was questioned at the Budapest Police Investigations Department on suspicion of tax fraud and the breaching of accounting regulations in the recent controversy involving more than HUF 804 million of payments made to her by the State Privatisation and Holding Co. @
- Parliament passed a resolution under which the government will establish a public foundation to compensate Hungary's Jewish community.

- The Finance Ministry has initiated a disciplinary procedure against a department manager after the State Audit Office turned up irregularities in the loan, bank and debt consolidation programmes carried out between 1992 and 1994.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and visiting Slovene Premier Janez Drnovsek signed an agreement in Budapest on Tuesday to build a railway line between the two countries. @

- Authorities arrested a 17-year-old secondary school student Monday night in his flat in Esztergom for being behind the recent explosion of a ketchup bottle in a food store and masterminding a recent bus blast in Piliscsaba.

- The US Embassy in Budapest on Tuesday roundly rejected charges published by the daily Uj Magyarorszag saying neither the embassy nor the US government have expressed dissatisfaction with Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
- Ferencvaros beat Newcastle United by 3-2 in a UEFA Cup first-leg soccer match on Tuesday.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal accompanied by MPs flew to Dublin on Monday for a three-day official visit.
- The Central Fund for Environmental Protection made public a list of the 89 environmental protection projects on Tuesday that have won central budget subsidies totalling HUF 1.7 billion.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The construction sector produced 3 percent less in volume terms in August compared to the same month last year, the Central Statistical Office reports. @
- More than 100 people from Africa have been detained in recent days for illegally entering Hungary, the UN High Commissioner's Office for Refugees said.
- An exhibition to commemorate the 1956 Hungarian uprising opens at the French Institute in Budapest today.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- One of the world's largest manufacturers of steel construction beams, America's Butler Manufacturing Company will purchase 55 percent of Beker Mernoki Kft. of Nyiregyhaza on December 1, Butler President Richard O. Ballentine said. @
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. suspended the allocation of shares of the five gas suppliers to local councils yesterday.
